newsitem.title: UK: UK regulator has "about 80" responses to metals review.
newsitem.headline: UK regulator has "about 80" responses to metals review.

text.p: Britain's top financial watchdog, the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said on Monday it has received "about 80" responses to its 33-question document sent out as part of its review of the base metals market set up in June.
The top to bottom review of the non-ferrous metals market followed the admission by Japan's Sumitomo Corp that it had made huge losses, now estimated at $2.6 billion, in unauthorised copper trading.
"We have received about 80 responses (to the document)," said an SIB spokesman.
The deadline for responses was October 15.
The SIB sent out around 3,500 questionnaires to users of the London Metal Exchange (LME) around the world.
The spokesman said the level of response was not disappointing despite the fact that some metal traders said they had expected it to be much higher.
"I don't think we are disappointed at all," he said.

"Some responses come from organisations, for example the IWCC (International Wrought Copper Council), which represent a lot more people, so some people will be having their responses done collectively," the spokesman added.
He said that the make-up of the LME's board of directors, currently made up mostly of LME ring dealing members, was a major area of concern among the LME's users.
"There was an open-ended question which allowed people to comment on what they wanted to, and I think that almost without exception people raised the issue of LME governance," he said.
The spokesman said the results of the SIB review will be made known in December.
